result.notes:
1) The tree moved while I was scanning. The worktree branch wip/r2-int was merged from origin/claude/r3-followups (426a1d0 → 60e527c), and origin/main is now v0.19.0, not v0.18.0. All line numbers and counts are re-pinned to 60e527c. That merge added one meta key, warp.skills (pkg/runs/runs.go:116), and a scope warning (internal/app/config.go:775-781 machineWarnings), both included above. Re-run the greps on the commit the rename actually starts from. No HTTP headers, user agent, ID prefixes, journal or store key prefixes, or state namespaces contain warp; the 22 namespaces are plain words such as runs, clients and schedules. ~/.warp and /etc/warp are never read by Go; /etc/warp appears only in the compose file Go writes.

2) There is no single place env is read. The closest seam is `getenv := overlay(file.env, os.Getenv)` in internal/app/main.go:227 inside serve(), but about 14 reads bypass it: main.go:111 (authz), 170 (addStateFlags), 302 (cfg.Env=os.LookupEnv for client env: references), 349 (WARP_AGENT_MODEL); start.go:59-60; setup.go:27; config.go:722,744,788; deploy.go:58,229 (os.Environ to docker compose), 572; pkg/credref/credref.go:130 (env: references); statetest.go:60. Recommended single choke point: at the top of app.Execute (internal/app/main.go:85, the entry for every subcommand), for each WARP_X in os.Environ() with HUMAGEN_X unset, call os.Setenv("HUMAGEN_X", v). Collect those names and print one stderr warning per old name, plus one when both are set and differ. Never unset WARP_X, because stored client and person references name WARP_* variables by exact name. Then switch every constant to HUMAGEN_*, and switch the overlay keys config.go writes from the spec. This shim must ship together with the sign-in secret exclusion fix (EnvRef accepts both prefixes; every WARP_OIDC check also covers HUMAGEN_OIDC), or it creates a secret-exfiltration hole.

3) Persisted names fall into three tiers. Keep forever: the advisory lock value, warp_state (unless doing a no-rollback migration), the compose volume, Postgres role and database, and the built-in agent handles. Accept both and write the new one: api_version, warp_client/warp_token, the scope prefix, group defaults, the review format id, the env prefix, person reference starts, the config file and directories, and the workspace directory. Free to rename: cookies (sessions are in memory), mock IdP names, WARP_REF_n, test env, copy. For the 23 tag-meta keys, keeping the strings is the cheapest fully compatible choice. If they change, read through a single helper that falls back on key absence, and delete both old and new keys at every strip or overwrite point, so untrusted tags cannot smuggle an old key past admission (warp.skills, warp.within and warp.sources are the dangerous ones).

4) Couplings in other areas that must move in the same change: Dockerfile paths (/var/lib/warp, /etc/warp, /usr/share/warp/web, /usr/local/bin/warp, XDG_CACHE_HOME); deploy/helm/warp directory and chart names; apps/slack/src/config.ts env names; apps/slack/manifest.json golden file; api/openapi.yaml cookie docs; Makefile, CI, deploy/helm/check.sh and apps/slack/src/warp.server.test.ts `./cmd/warp`; pnpm @warp/* scope in the main.go:225 message; docs/security.md group names.

Existing releases are named warp: docs/deploy.md:157 'helm install warp deploy/helm/warp -n warp', the Flux HelmRelease 'warp', and warp deploy's default release (the System metadata.name, default 'warp'). Today fullname is 'warp'; with the new chart name it becomes 'warp-humagen', because 'humagen' is not contained in 'warp'.
